title: Core banking modernisation
businessObjective: Modernise a legacy core-banking estate through governed coexistence and migration with minimal customer disruption and reversible transition states.

requirements.statement: Preserve channel access to customer, account, payment and product capabilities throughout migration.
Integrate product processing with the general ledger and regulatory reporting.
Support coexistence routing between legacy and target cores by governed migration state.
Reconcile data and financial postings before, during and after every migration wave.
Support controlled cutover, rollback and exception handling.
Migrate batch workloads and end-of-day dependencies without losing operational control.
Minimise customer disruption and define measurable transition service levels.
Preserve security, auditability and segregation of duties across coexistence.
Contain operational and data-integrity risk with rehearsed recovery paths.
Observe business reconciliation and technical health across both estates.
The legacy core cannot be replaced in a single big-bang event.
Regulatory and general-ledger obligations remain authoritative throughout transition.

constraints: Legacy interfaces and batch windows have incomplete documentation.
Customer and account migration ordering is constrained by product dependencies.
assumptions: A migration control plane can hold account-level migration state.
Parallel reconciliation can compare legacy and target outcomes.
